label: copy-phase input s (fed back) at recall positions 3-4 in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps whose input is the token s (99.5% of activation mass), meaning the model has just emitted s and is now recalling the original token right after it. It is strongly position-gated: almost all mass falls at recall_idx 3-4 (s was originally at position 2-3) in sequences of length 7-9. The strongest activations are s at original position 2 in L=9 sequences (t=12, five outputs still to go), and magnitude rises with L. It is near zero or silent for s in short sequences (L<=6), for s copied early (recall_idx<=2) or late (recall_idx>=6), and for s during the original phase or at the delimiter. It essentially never fires on other tokens. A repeated s directly after the first one gets a weaker activation. Dev: P 0.83, R 0.76, F1 0.79, mass recall 0.91.

issues: Reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.823, R 0.763, F1 0.792, mass recall 0.914.

The factual claims hold. Activation is 100% in the copy phase, with zero in the original phase and at the delimiter. in_tok s carries 99.5% of mass, and other tokens fire only scattered (61 or fewer steps each). recall_idx 3 and 4 carry 57.7% and 36.8% of mass. L=9 carries 54% of mass, and magnitude rises with L. L<=5 is effectively silent (mass 0.002), and recall_idx<=2 and >=6 are near silent (mass about 0.01 each). to_go 0-1 is near silent.

Precision varies with length inside the predicate. In the L=9 cells precision is 0.997 (recall_idx 3) and 0.94 (recall_idx 4). In the L=8 cells it is 0.94 and 0.82. In the L=7 cells it drops to 0.69 and 0.53. So most of the 2947 false positives come from L=7. This matches the claim that strength is graded by L. It is not a separate missing class.

The missed activations (8.6% of mass) are weak, low-magnitude tails of the same s-in-copy-phase pattern: recall_idx 5 (mass 0.036), L=6 (mass 0.022) and recall_idx 2 (0.011). Every variant I tried that widens or narrows the predicate (recall_idx 3-5, L>=6, L>=8, L>=8 or L=7 with recall_idx 3, excluding a preceding s) lowers test F1 (0.70-0.78). No better predicate found.
The claim that a second s gives a weaker activation is supported: inside the predicate, precision is 0.61 when prev_tok==s versus 0.83 otherwise.

Minor: F1 of 0.79 sits just under the 0.8 cutoff. The verdict 'explained' rests on mass recall 0.91 and high precision for L>=8. That is acceptable, but the label could mention the graded fall-off at L=7.
